title: On Condition That
gist_ar: نص عن صياغة العقود: الشرط اللي مش مكتوب بيبقى واجب على الطرف الأضعف.
text:
A grant agreement is a machine for allocating uncertainty, and it works only
insofar as every condition in it is attached to somebody who can satisfy it.
Provided that this holds, the document is a genuine allocation of risk. Where it
does not, the risk has not disappeared; it has simply been left where it fell.

Consider a clause of a familiar type. Funds are released on condition that
construction begins within twelve months, unless delay is attributable to
regulatory approval, in which case the period is extended. Supposing the approval
takes fourteen months — as it did — the extension is triggered and nobody is at
fault. So far the machine works.

Now consider what the agreement did not stipulate. Assuming, as both parties
evidently did, that the contractor's price would hold for those fourteen months,
no provision was made for the eventuality that it would not. But for that
omission, the escalation would have been a shared contingency. As long as it went
unmentioned, it remained wholly with the recipient, who had no means of hedging
it and no standing to renegotiate.

This is the general form of the problem. A condition that is written is a
condition that has been priced by somebody. A prerequisite that is merely
presupposed is subject to no such discipline, and it will hinge on whichever
party is least able to walk away.

Given that drafting time is finite, the practical counsel is narrow: for every
assumption on which the schedule depends, ask who bears it if it fails. Were the
answer to be "the weaker party, by default", the clause has not been drafted. It
has been declined, and the reciprocal obligation everyone believes they signed
does not exist.

questions.q: What does the writer say a grant agreement is for?
questions.q_ar: اتفاقية التمويل موجودة ليه حسب الكاتب؟
options: Protecting the funder's contribution against any conceivable escalation in cost
Allocating uncertainty to whoever can satisfy each condition

questions.q: Which risk was left entirely with the recipient?
questions.q_ar: أنهي مخاطرة وقعت بالكامل على المستفيد؟

questions.q: What is the difference between a written and a presupposed condition?
questions.q_ar: إيه الفرق بين شرط مكتوب وشرط مفترض؟
options: A written one is legally binding, a presupposed one is moral
A written one has been priced by somebody; a presupposed one has not

questions.q: What test does the writer recommend when drafting?
questions.q_ar: إيه الاختبار اللي بينصح بيه عند الصياغة؟
options: Count the conditions and make sure each one has been formally priced by the funder
Ask who bears each assumption if it fails
Have a lawyer review every clause
